Israel has been completed without holy prophets. They became captives at times and went to the land of the Persians and Medes with their wives and loved ones. However, they did not go down to Egypt without holy prophets, after the Babylonians had taken Jerusalem, but the prophet Jeremiah was with them, serving them with words from God. Since they have been persuaded to Christ, they have been deserted and their entire security has fallen. I think this is what it means to say that their wall has been torn down. The word of the holy prophets has ceased, and their voices have been silenced. I think this is what was said to them by God: 'Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will bring a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread or thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.' They will run from east to west seeking the word of the Lord, but they will not find it. This has happened to the Israelites, and quite rightly so. For they rejected the Lord of powers, who nourishes souls and hearts with spiritual showers. David also remembered this, saying: 'Like the dew of Hermon coming down upon the mountains of Zion.' But a new vineyard has been raised up instead, that of those called to sanctification through faith. The Bridegroom from heaven, that is, Christ, says about them: 'The vines are in bloom, they have given fragrance.'

He himself is the first and all-holy and true vine, and we have been separated from him like branches, being filled with his life-giving nourishment, and he says clearly, 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer,' and every branch in him not bearing fruit he removes, and every branch bearing fruit he prunes, so that it may bear more fruit, and since we have been grafted to him through intimacy, it is clear that we have become fruitful, and he himself teaches us to remain in him, saying, 'Remain in me, and I in you,' and just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can we unless we remain in him, and he says, 'I am the vine, you are the branches,' and the one remaining in him, and he in him, bears much fruit, because apart from him we can do nothing, and so it is necessary to be grafted to the true vine, that is, Christ, through faith and love and obedience to everything, and he himself will declare us fruitful, and he will put a fence around us, and raise up the wall, and separate us
pass_b_english: The Israelites have been completed without holy prophets.
At various times, they were taken captive and forced to flee to the lands of the Persians and Medes, accompanied by their wives and loved ones.
However, when they went down to Egypt, they were not without the prophetic guidance of Jeremiah, who served them with words from God, after the Babylonians had taken Jerusalem.
Since they have been persuaded to Christ, they have been abandoned and their security has been shattered, which, I believe, is what is meant by the statement that their wall has been torn down.
The prophetic voice that once guided them has fallen silent, and the word of the holy prophets has ceased to be spoken.

I think this is what God meant when He said, 'Behold, days are coming when I will bring a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread or thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord' (Amos 8:11-12).
They will run from east to west seeking the word of the Lord, but they will not find it.

This has happened to them, and it is only fitting, for they rejected the Lord of powers, who nourishes souls and hearts with spiritual showers, as the psalmist David remembered, saying, 'Like the dew of Hermon coming down upon the mountains of Zion' (Psalm 133:3).

But a new vineyard has been raised up, one that consists of those who have been called to sanctification through faith, and the Bridegroom from heaven, Christ, says of them, 'The vines are in bloom, they have given fragrance'.
Christ himself is the all-holy, the true vine, and we have been separated from him like branches, being filled with his life-giving nourishment.

He clearly says, 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer' (John 15:1), and every branch in him that does not bear fruit, he removes, and every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, so that it may bear more fruit.
Since we have been grafted to him through intimacy, it is clear that we have become fruitful, and he teaches us to remain in him, saying, 'Remain in me, and I in you' (John 15:4).

Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can we unless we remain in him, and he says, 'I am the vine, you are the branches' (John 15:5), and the one remaining in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because apart from him, we can do nothing.

Therefore, it is necessary to be grafted to the true vine, that is, Christ, through faith and love and obedience to everything, and he himself will declare us fruitful, and he will put a fence around us, and raise up the wall, and separate us.
